title: 2 John

stories.title: 📜 2 John
summaryBullets: The elder, To the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in the truth — and not I alone, but also all who know the truth — (1:1).
because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever: (1:2).
Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, will be with us in truth and love. (1:3).
I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us. (1:4).
And now I urge you, dear lady — not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning — that we love one another. (1:5).
And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the very commandment you have heard from the beginning, that you must walk in love. (1:6).
For many deceivers have gone out into the world, refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Any such person is the deceiver and the antichrist. (1:7).
Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded. (1:8).
Anyone who runs ahead without remaining in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son. (1:9).
If anyone comes to you but does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your home or even greet him. (1:10).
Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds. (1:11).
I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with paper and ink. Instead, I hope to come and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete. (1:12).
The children of your elect sister send you greetings. (1:13).
crossRefs: John 14:6 — Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life.
3 John 1:4 — Joy that children walk in the truth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הָאִשָּׁה הַנִּבְחֶרֶת (hāʾiššāh hannibḥéreṯ, sense) — Greek: ἐκλεκτῇ κυρίᾳ (eklektē kyría, NT) — Aramaic: אתתא בחירתא (ʾettatā baḥīrtā)
translationNotes.note: Likely refers to a specific woman believer and her household, though some interpret it figuratively of a church; literally means 'chosen lady.'

stories.keyTakeaway: John greets the elect lady and her children with love in truth, affirming grace, mercy, and peace, and rejoicing in their faithful walk.

intro:
2 John is only 13 verses, one of the shortest books in the Bible. The author identifies himself as 'the elder,' a common self-reference of John in his later years. The letter is addressed to 'the elect lady and her children', most likely a particular local church and its members, though some read it as written to a literal woman.

The occasion is the same false teaching addressed in 1 John: itinerant teachers were going from house church to house church spreading denials of Christ's incarnation. The letter has two main concerns: keep walking in love (verses 4-6) and do not extend hospitality to deceivers (verses 7-11). Both concerns flow from the same conviction; truth and love are inseparable, and Christian hospitality must not be deployed in service of teaching that undermines the gospel.

John ends the letter abruptly: he hopes to visit in person and speak face to face rather than write more on paper and ink. Despite its brevity, 2 John encapsulates the church's perennial duty: extend hospitality generously, but not at the cost of welcoming destructive doctrine into the body.
